vsExpectations.text: Large beat: revenue Rs5,033cr vs consensus Rs4,263cr (Bajaj) / Rs4,260cr (PL) and PL est Rs4,281cr; EBITDA Rs1,237cr vs consensus Rs917cr (Bajaj) and PL est Rs951cr (+30%); PAT Rs759cr vs PL est Rs530cr (+43%). Gross margin 51.2% (incl. inventory gains).

drivers.text: Chemicals: fluorochemicals strong on healthy domestic demand and robust exports; higher volumes in refrigerants, industrial chemicals and fluoropolymers plus better realisations offset raw-material inflation from supply-chain disruption; HFC plants at high utilisation; Middle East volumes and pricing very robust in Q1 after Q4 disruption ('Floron commands differentiated pricing'). Specialty: 'steady' but pricing pressure from Chinese competition continues; early volume uptick and marginal price improvement in core products; some opportunistic buying.

Performance Films & Foil: best-ever quarter; Middle East war shut competitor capacity while SRF ran at 100% (DTA unit, global raw-material sourcing); customer panic buying lifted prices; CFO: 'In a perverse way, the war has helped us'. Overseas units (South Africa, Thailand, Hungary) all improved. Foil: close to half of Q1 volume went to Europe.

Technical Textiles: demand recovery supported by inventory gains; belting exports to US after tariff rationalisation; PIY share gains (geotextile, seatbelt) helped by QCO stay order from May-2026; difficulty renegotiating spreads early in the quarter.
Below the line: ECF (forex) loss Rs102cr vs Rs8.7cr gain in Q1FY26. CMD Ashish Bharat Ram: 'best-ever quarterly performance'; 'inventory gains provided some support during the June quarter'.

guidanceAsStated.text: 15-20% guidance held; 'Hopefully, we will eventually land at the higher end of that by the end of the year, given how strong Q1 has been.'
Chemicals highly seasonal; Q2 lower than Q1 sequentially but growth YoY.

Ref-gas pricing expected to stay at current levels or get better; Q2/Q3 weaker than Q1 for India and Middle East in both volume and price, but strong YoY growth in Q2; China pricing to hold at least to FY27 end; quota-related outcomes through December 'significantly positive'. Deck: stable demand-price environment globally; focus on maximising HFC production and capacity expansion; prolonged Middle East conflict may pressure key raw materials; chloromethanes range-bound.

Green shoots in volume and price on core products; 'scraped the bottom'; recovery 'linear and probably slow', not a hockey stick; H2 stronger than H1. 6-7 innovator AIs: capacity and chemistry ready, but launch depends on innovator registrations - timelines 'uncertain at this point to say it mildly'. Pharma target 20-30% (of specialty revenue) by 2030; deck: new launches planned in coming quarters; generics pressure on agro innovators continues. Dahej has space for specialty growth for ~24 months.

Q1 'is an aberration. Do not peg it over there'; Q2 to stabilise at more normal levels, no 'steep cliff'; baseline margin to be north of the historical 8-12% EBIT range (overseas turnaround + VAP mix). Crude ~US$70 supportive. Deck: BOPET/BOPP demand to revert to normal as customers rationalise inventories; Thailand hit by ocean freight surge; Hungary holiday slowdown Aug-26; new metallizers (Thailand, South Africa) and offline coater (India) to cushion.
Already ramped up; ~half of volume to Europe; aseptic-packaging approvals could open a new segment from early FY28; no foil capacity expansion 'on the cards' (Jetapur site has space).
Q2 to normalise but improve YoY; TCF demand flat to marginally positive; new dipping line to lift share; belting exports to grow; PIY stable.
~Rs2,500cr maintained (ICICI Direct summary of call). New: Rs250cr BOPET thick-film line 25,000 tpa (India), ~24 months, debt + accruals.

Odisha projects (HFO, backward integration, specialty fluoropolymers) progressing to plan; site regulatory approvals being applied for; post-HFO SRF to be top 3-4 refrigerant makers globally. Prior guidance (6-May-2026): ~Rs2,300cr (board Rs22.85bn) over 2 years for 20,000 tpa HFO + 30,000 tpa HF + EHF; commissioning 'Feb 2028 potential timeline'.
Plant 'set to be commissioned towards the end of this quarter' (i.e. by Sep-2026); meaningful volumes/realisations from start of FY28.

Chemours requested design changes and specific European equipment; FP3/FP4 could move out '3, 4 months versus the December timelines'; return-on-investment style contract; revenue within first year of commissioning; FY28 lower, full stream FY29.
PTFE value-added grades to show meaningful scale end-Q4FY27 / early Q1FY28; whole fluoropolymer portfolio meaningful volumes end FY28 / early FY29, full stream during FY29.
